claims.text: Silicon carbide ceramic can be used to prepare parts for hot-dip aluminum dipping and plating equipment.
Silicon carbide protects dipping and plating equipment from erosion by high-temperature liquid aluminum.
The proposed starting material is polished silicon carbide ceramic.
The proposed exposure is immersion in liquid aluminum at 700°C for 100 hours.
The proposed immersion occurs in an inert atmosphere without external mechanical stress.
A thin, dense alumina layer forms on the SiC surface during exposure.
The surface alumina layer acts as a barrier between liquid aluminum and SiC.
The alumina barrier prevents liquid aluminum from reacting with SiC.
Preventing reaction between liquid aluminum and SiC reduces erosion.
SiC will exhibit at least a 90% lower erosion rate than unprotected steel under the same conditions.
The target erosion rate for SiC is less than 0.1 mm/year.
Unprotected steel, such as AISI 1020, is the proposed comparison control.
SiC performance may vary with SiC material properties, surface finish, and process conditions.
The formation and stability of the alumina layer may depend on temperature, atmosphere, and aluminum-alloy composition.
The hypothesis is designated as falsified if SiC erosion is not at least 80% lower than steel erosion.

contradictions.description: The prediction requires at least a 90% erosion reduction, whereas the falsification rule only rejects results below an 80% reduction. Results from 80% up to but below 90% would fail the stated prediction without falsifying the hypothesis under the stated rule.
